subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — GPU comparison & decision logbook

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo recap & performance questions (dedicated sizing)

Thanks again for today's demo — good conversation. I wanted to capture the practical performance/size items we discussed so we have a clear decision path for a Dedicated pilot. Short version up front: we recommend a brief benchmarking pilot across two GPU profiles (H100 / L40S), reserve a small pool, and validate against your P95 latency and burst throughput targets before committing to a larger reserved pool.

Key notes from the call (please correct me if I got anything wrong):
- Target SLOs: P95 latency <= 350ms for median chat requests (~150 tokens), time-to-first-token (TTFT) for streaming <= 150ms.
- Traffic profile: average sustained QPS ~80 requests/sec, expected peak bursts up to ~220 QPS, ~180 concurrent streams during peaks.
- Payload: average response ~150 tokens; 15% of requests are long context (>1024 tokens) and need KV cache benefits.
- Availability: you asked for a 99.9% uptime objective on the Dedicated pool for core API calls.

Recommended pilot outline (for alignment):
1) Two-arm pilot (2–3 days each): H100 x4 and L40S x4 reserved pools, run synthetic and replayed traffic (we'll supply load scripts).
2) Reserved throughput target for each arm: 120 sustained RPS with 30% headroom (so plan for 160 RPS burst).
3) Metrics to capture: P50/P95/P99 latency, TTFT (streaming), token/sec, GPU utilization, memory pressure, cache hit rate, and cost/tok.
4) Acceptance criteria: P95 <= 350ms (non-streaming) and TTFT <= 150ms for >=90% of streaming traces at peak burst.

Open questions we need from your side to size the pilot: (a) confirm peak burst duration (typical burst window: 5–15 minutes?), (b) confirm SLA-critical routes (which endpoints must remain on Dedicated), (c) internal procurement timeline for a short-term reserved pilot.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-matrix.xlsx (pilot plan & cost estimates) and mutual-action-plan-orion-2026.docx (starter MAP).

Next steps I propose: Jordan to provision test pools & load harness; Karthik to draft exact test scripts; Max/Sofia to confirm burst window and routes by end of week.

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & performance questions (dedicated sizing)

Thanks Jordan — great summary. A few clarifications from our engineering side: 
- Peak bursts are typically short, ~8–12 minutes, tied to morning syncs and batch uploads. We sometimes see a second smaller burst in the late afternoon (~4–6 minutes).
- SLA-critical routes: /chat/generate (most traffic), /chat/stream (real-time clients), and /embed/bulk (background processing; can be lower priority).
- Long-context requests occur mainly in clinical note stitching workflows and are ~8% of traffic during business hours (lower at night).

On the pilot: procurement is okay to sign a short-term reserved pilot (60 days) but needs a clear cancellation clause; procurement@orionhealth.ai is looped for contract language.

One ask: can you include a lightweight runbook for graceful degradation in the pilot (what fallback behavior you recommend if the Dedicated pool reaches capacity)? That will be important for our SREs.

Appreciate the attachments. We'll try to return the confirmation on burst window and critical endpoints by Thursday.

—Max

Thanks — adding the technical validation plan and a short GPU comparison so everyone has the tradeoffs in one place. High level guidance below; I'll follow up with the test scripts and the concrete measurement workbook.

Pilot hardware choices (pros/cons):
- NVIDIA H100 (large): best raw throughput and future-proofing for larger context windows; higher cost but smaller cluster needed for same RPS. Ideal if you expect increased long-context traffic and heavy batching.
- NVIDIA L40S / L40S-PCIe: lower unit cost, good for high-concurrency streaming; may need more GPUs to hit the same sustained RPS for large models. Good fit if cost per token is the primary constraint and your average context sizes remain moderate.
- A100 80GB (if available): solid middle ground for memory-heavy models, but H100 usually wins on throughput for fp16 ops.

Quantization & model variants: running an 8-bit/4-bit quantized variant can reduce memory and increase throughput; we should validate quality on your prompt sets (we'll include eval delta tracking).

Pilot sizing proposal (conservative):
- Reserve 4 GPUs per arm (H100 x4 vs L40S x4). We'll provision an autoscaling buffer for short bursts (unreserved pool or burst credits).
- Target reserved sustained throughput: 120 RPS (this should cover your sustained + baseline headroom). Configure for 200 RPS burst capacity via temporary burst pool or rapid autoscale.
- Concurrency testing: simulate 150–250 concurrent open streaming sessions with a TTFT target <=150ms.

Validation plan (metrics & tests):
1) Synthetic replay using 72K traces from your anonymized replay + synthetic long-context traces at 1x/3x peak.
2) Run each arm through a 4-hour sustained test + two 15-minute burst windows at 200 RPS.
3) Capture: P50/P95/P99 latency, TTFT, token/sec, GPU utilization, memory headroom, cache hit rate, error/saturation events, and cost/tok.
4) Post-test: run quality regression evals over the same prompts to ensure quantized models meet acceptance thresholds.

Runbook (short):
- Preferred fallback: route degraded load to a cheaper compatible model variant (lower precision / smaller context) with a de-prioritized SLA for non-critical endpoints (/embed/bulk).
- If Dedicated pool saturates: (1) return HTTP 429 with Retry-After for best-effort clients; (2) for low-latency streaming clients, auto-failover to Hosted tier for a subset of calls (requires egress policy & throttling). We'll draft the exact policy and canned responses for SREs.

Next steps I will own: a) deliver the exact load scripts and measurement workbook by Monday, Nov 9; b) confirm config for burst pool/autoscale; c) coordinate quantized-model evals.

-Karthik
